answer: Business process automation (BPA) is using software to run a complete business process, such as onboarding a client or paying a supplier, from start to finish with minimal manual work. Modern BPA combines workflow tools with AI, so steps that once needed a person to read or decide can also be automated.
body:
Why automate whole processes, not just tasks

Many businesses already have a few automations: a form that emails a manager, a spreadsheet that totals itself. The real cost sits in the gaps between them. Someone still copies data from email into the CRM, chases a missing signature, re-keys an invoice or checks three systems to answer one question. Business process automation looks at the whole journey, from the moment work arrives to the moment it’s done, and fixes the hand-offs where time and errors pile up.

Automating a single task can save minutes. Automating a whole process usually saves hours per week per person, cuts error rates and makes the work visible, so managers can see where every job is up to without asking.

Our approach: map, redesign, automate, measure

  1. Map the current process. We sit with the people who do the work and document every step, tool, decision and exception, including the workarounds nobody wrote down.
  2. Redesign it. We remove duplicate steps, unnecessary approvals and re-keying before anything is automated. Automating a bad process just makes mistakes faster.
  3. Automate in stages. Rules handle predictable steps, AI handles reading and judgement, and people keep the decisions that matter. We release in small stages so your team can adjust.
  4. Measure and improve. We record time and error rates before and after, and report monthly on hours saved, exceptions and what we tuned.

Processes we commonly automate

ProcessTypical manual stepsWhat automation does
Client onboardingForms, ID checks, contracts, account set-up, welcome emailsCollects details once, sends documents for e-signature, creates records in every system
Procure to payPurchase orders, invoice entry, approvals, payment runsAI reads invoices, matches to orders, routes approvals, prepares payment batches
Lead to quoteEnquiry triage, follow-up, quoting, CRM updatesInstant replies, lead scoring, quote drafts and CRM updates
Job managementBooking, scheduling, reminders, job sheets, invoicingBookings flow into schedules, job sheets become invoices automatically
Staff onboardingPaperwork, accounts, training, equipmentChecklists, account creation and reminders triggered from one form
Compliance reportingCollecting data from several systems each monthData pulled, checked and summarised on schedule

Where AI fits in process automation

Traditional automation struggles with anything unstructured: emails, PDFs, scanned forms and free-text notes. That’s where AI changes what is possible. Our automations use AI to read documents and extract the right fields, classify incoming requests, draft replies and summaries, and spot unusual cases that need a person. For document-heavy steps, see document and data processing.

AI never gets the final say on high-risk actions. Payments, contracts and anything customer-facing above a set risk level wait for human approval, and every automated step is logged.

Tools and platforms

We work with the software you already have and add the minimum new tooling needed. Orchestration usually runs on n8n, Make or Power Automate, connected to systems such as Xero, MYOB, HubSpot, Zoho, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and industry software. For the details of workflow platforms, see AI workflow automation; for sales and customer records, see CRM automation.

Governance and privacy

Process automation often moves personal and financial information between systems. We design every process around the Privacy Act 1988 and follow the OAIC’s guidance on commercially available AI products. Each automated process comes with a one-page summary: what it does, which data it touches, who owns it and what happens when something goes wrong.

What results look like

Results depend on the process, volume and starting point, so we measure rather than promise. Before building, we time the current process and count how often it runs. After launch you get a monthly report with runs completed, hours saved, errors caught and exceptions handled. For a quick estimate before talking to us, use the automation savings calculator.

How a business process automation project runs

  1. Free AI audit to choose the process with the best payback.
  2. Process mapping workshop on site in Melbourne or by video.
  3. Redesign and fixed quote in AUD, with the future process documented.
  4. Staged build and testing on real cases, usually three to six weeks.
  5. Launch, training and monthly improvement.

Not sure which process to start with? Our AI Readiness Assessment ranks your candidates by payback and risk.
faqs: What is the difference between business process automation and workflow automation?

Workflow automation connects tools to run a sequence of steps. Business process automation is broader: it redesigns and automates an entire process across teams, often using several workflows, AI steps and human approval points together.
Which business processes should we automate first?

Start with processes that run often, follow a mostly consistent pattern, involve re-keying data between systems and cost real time each week. Client onboarding, invoice processing and lead follow-up are common first choices.
Do we need new software for business process automation?
Usually not. We automate around the systems you already use and add an orchestration tool such as n8n or Make where needed. We only recommend new software when it clearly pays for itself.
How long does a business process automation project take?
A single well-defined process usually takes three to six weeks from mapping to launch. Larger programs across several departments are delivered in stages over two to three months.
